text:
maria: FYI customer hit a burst of 502/504s hitting /v1/stream during a model swap in eu1 ~ 10:12-10:20 UTC. They say it only affects streaming, non-streaming calls fine.

sam: Can you paste a sample trace_id or curl they used?

maria: trace: trace_eu_000112233. Customer repro: long-lived HTTP/2 stream, chunked audio frames. Example they shared: ```curl -v --http2 -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cust" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" \
  --data-binary @audio_chunk.bin \
  https://api.eu1.redwood.ai/v1/stream```

jordan: Checked envoy logs around that trace: we're seeing repeated `http2: stream reset: REFUSED_STREAM` and `max_concurrent_streams` warnings on frontdoor -> midproxy. Snippet: ```[envoy][warning] upstream reset: code=REFUSED_STREAM reason=max_concurrent_streams exceeded```

eng-runtime: That pattern looks like H2 stream concurrency exhaustion during concurrent reconnects. During model swap backends drain and clients re-establish streams; if many long-lived streams reconnect at once we hit the h2 SETTINGS limit. When upstream returns REFUSED_STREAM, client (our frontdoor) retries and sometimes gets 504/502 if retries amplify and backend pool is temporarily small.

li: Quick mitigation options: 1) increase `max_concurrent_streams` on frontdoor->midproxy path (envoy/h2 settings) 2) enable connection warmup routing to prefer warm instances during swap 3) add a per-tenant streaming concurrency cap to throttle reconnect storms.

maria: Customer willing to try a reduced concurrency test. They can limit parallel streams from their side to 4 and retest. Meanwhile can we try increasing h2 max streams from 100 -> 300 on a single midproxy node in eu1 canary?

sam: I'll prepare an envoy config patch and run canary on midproxy-02. Patch will set `http2_protocol_options: { max_concurrent_streams: 300 }` and tune `initial_window_size`.

jordan: Also recommend setting `retry_policy` to avoid aggressive immediate retries for REFUSED_STREAM. Add small random jitter backoff. That prevents retry amplification during drain.

eng-runtime: Agreed. I'll queue a runtime rollout: bump max_concurrent_streams on 2 midproxy nodes (canary then rollback window). If canary looks clean for 10m we can roll rest.

ops-bot: Deployment scheduled: env-midproxy-config/2026-03-20T10:40Z -> canary midproxy-02 (eu1). Pause window 10m. CI diff: https://ci.redwood/changes/ENV-4373

maria: Customer will throttle to 4 parallel streams and try again at 10:50 UTC.

sam: If we still see errors after max_streams bump, we should capture a tcpdump + h2 debug on frontdoor and midproxy to confirm SETTINGS frames and stream count at failure. Command: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/h2.pcap port 443` then use `nghttp` to inspect.

li: Note: this change increases memory per connection on midproxy. We'll monitor memory and QPS. Watchlist: `envoy.http2.stream_count`, `upstream_cx_total`, `envoy.cluster.upstream_rq_5xx`.

maria: Thanks. Will update customer once the canary is green. :thumbsup:

jordan: I'll run the canary now, ping when done.

maria: Awesome — keep me posted, will attach customer repro logs as they come.

eng-runtime: Can confirm canary applied to midproxy-02 at 10:43 UTC, no immediate 5xx spike in that node logs for 12m. Continuing rollout to midproxy-03.

maria: Customer retested with 4 parallel streams at 10:56 UTC and reports no 502/504s in their sample window. They're running longer soak now.

sam: Leaving this open as a post-deploy task: create defensive change to retry jitter + per-tenant streaming caps and add a small preroll warmup during model swap.

maria: Agreed. Filing follow-up RFC for warmup + caps. Thanks team. :eyes:
